question: At the 36th National Games, Hashika Ramchandra won six gold medals in which of the following sports?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Swimming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Hashika Ramchandra is a young and talented swimmer who made a remarkable achievement in the 36th National Games.

• She won a total of six gold medals in various swimming events, showcasing her versatility and dominance in the sport.

• The National Games is a prestigious multi-sport event in India, where athletes from different states compete.

• Hashika's performance in swimming contributed significantly to her team's overall medal tally in the National Games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **National Games of India**

• The National Games of India is a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from the Indian states and union territories.

• The first modern National Games on the lines of the Olympics were held in 1924 in Lahore, British India.

• These games are organized by the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).

• The National Games aim to promote and develop sports at the grass-root level across the country.

• **Swimming in India**

• Swimming is a popular competitive sport in India, and it includes different styles like freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly.

• India has produced several notable swimmers who have represented the country at international competitions like the Commonwealth Games, Asian Games, and the Olympics.

• The Swimming Federation of India (SFI) is the governing body for swimming in India.

• Training for competitive swimming involves rigorous practice, strength training, and maintaining a balanced diet.

• **Key Terminologies in Swimming**

• **Freestyle**: A swimming style where the swimmer is free to use any stroke, but the front crawl is most commonly used.
